clue.text: Gets as far as waking up?

definitions.meaning: to reach a point or total, as a bill reaching a sum

explanation.surface: A wry question about how far someone gets each morning: only to the point of waking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase has two idiomatic senses: reaching an amount or place, and recovering consciousness.

clue.text: Shellfish — 100 pounds a thousand

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's price list: shellfish at a hundred pounds per thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A clam is a bivalve mollusc, a common example of shellfish.

clue.text: All-round defence in depth?

parts.note: a castle's water-filled ditch defends it on every side, and is literally deep, punning on the military phrase 'defence in depth'

explanation.surface: Reads like a military strategy term for layered defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's encircling water-filled ditch protected it all round and had depth.

clue.text: Boys lost, misdirected by this mischievous fellow?

indicators.note: sent the wrong way, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Some lost boys were sent the wrong way by a prankster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, crafty or roguish person is jocularly called this, as in a mischievous trickster.

clue.text: Daisy is kind of neat to look at

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one kind
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a daisy is rather tidy to the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy', but here it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common wild flower, so the name alone denotes that daisy.

clue.text: Radio buff rented small place in the country

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast
let means rented out

explanation.surface: A radio enthusiast rents a cottage out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny rural settlement smaller than a village is this kind of place.

clue.text: One teaching at university is one that has to be fair

definitions.text: one that has to be fair

parts.note: a means one
a don is a university lecturer or fellow
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecturer is described as someone obliged to be impartial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' suggests fairness, but means good-looking here.
explanation.definitionFit: The handsome youth of Greek myth, whose name means a beautiful young man; fair means handsome.

clue.text: Profligate client settled debts

indicators.note: settled into a new arrangement, so the letters of client are reordered

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A wasteful client finally paid off what was owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe dissolute, unrestrained behaviour, especially in pleasure-seeking.

clue.text: Temple altar, perhaps, inlaid with nacre design

indicators.note: inlay sets material into a surface, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a communion table is an example of an altar

indicators.note: the word nacre is reworked into a new design

explanation.surface: A temple altar decorated with mother-of-pearl patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altar, perhaps' fits because a church altar is the communion table; 'design' is the anagram signal, not decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The portable sanctuary of the Israelites in the wilderness, a place of worship, is called by this name.

clue.text: Carefully examined any leads broken

indicators.note: the letters of any leads are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An investigator checked whether any clues had been cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something closely and methodically is to scrutinise it in detail.

clue.text: Young creature whose home is Earth

definitions.text: Young creature whose home is Earth

parts.words: Young creature whose home is Earth
parts.note: an earth is a fox's burrow, so the young animal living there is a baby fox

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of any newborn on our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's den is called an earth, and its offspring live there.

clue.text: New set admits another set in insect life

indicators.note: lets in, so one piece goes inside the other
a new version of the word set, with its letters rearranged

parts.note: a second copy of the word set, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh group takes in another group, among insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges SET into TSE, and SET goes in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness is a familiar form of insect.

clue.text: Change bowler — a very successful performer

parts.note: change means coins, i.e. money
a spinner is a cricket bowler who spins the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket captain switches bowlers and finds a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change bowler' reads as a cricket instruction; a spinner is a slow bowler who turns the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that earns a great deal of profit is called this, an idiom for a lucrative success.

clue.text: Jeopardise settlement

definitions.meaning: to put at risk, as in exposing someone's safety
an agreement where each side makes concessions

explanation.surface: Endangering a deal, perhaps by a hasty move.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both endangering something and a deal reached by mutual concession.

clue.text: Still a lack of variety

explanation.surface: Still, a lack of variety: a complaint about monotony.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'nevertheless' and 'identical in every case'.

clue.text: Bore a title difficult to get rid of

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are made into something awkward, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat once held a rank that was hard to shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or destroy completely is to eliminate something.

clue.text: Make someone take notice?

parts.note: reads as 'get attention', but means sign again, or hand in one's notice to quit a job

explanation.surface: Reads as a plea to get someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a job means giving notice; read as re-sign, it also means signing someone again.

clue.text: Girl Friday, no cook

indicators.note: without, so the letters of a word for cook are removed

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat

explanation.surface: An assistant, a Girl Friday, who cannot cook.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters F, R, Y are scattered through FRIDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a crossword's usual 'girl' sense.

clue.text: Not a difficult opponent to topple?

definitions.meaning: an easy adversary, someone easily beaten
to knock something over by shoving it

explanation.surface: An easy rival who would fall at a touch.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an easily defeated opponent; as two words it is to shove something down.

clue.text: Take a shot of cannabis

definitions.meaning: to sink a ball in snooker or billiards, or shoot game

explanation.surface: Someone takes a puff of a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both shooting or sinking a ball and is slang for marijuana.

clue.text: A son reading to secure university entrance — that's typical

indicators.note: to hold fast, so the reading holds a letter inside it

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A son studies hard to get into university, as you would expect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'as always', said of something predictably routine.

clue.text: Turn up in green

parts.note: taken as written
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone appears wearing green.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down is to flip it over.

clue.text: Deep study

parts.note: the deep is the sea, so this is the science of the oceans, not intense thought

explanation.surface: Reads as intense, profound concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific study of the seas, poetically called 'the deep'.

clue.text: A fight in the neighbourhood

parts.note: taken as written
a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out locally.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean nearby, as in 'is anyone around'.

clue.text: It has branches in every street

indicators.note: the four letters sit inside every instance of the word street

explanation.surface: A chain store with outlets on every high street.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant with a trunk and limbs, so branches are its defining feature.

clue.text: Finest — and worst!

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to defeat or get the better of

explanation.surface: An exclamation contrasting the top and the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the superlative of good, and also a verb meaning to defeat, as does 'worst'.

clue.text: Representations will be made, if game is disrupted

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Protests will follow if a match is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representations' suggests formal complaints, but here means pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures or likenesses are portrayals of something.

clue.text: Meet criminal by the roadside

parts.note: a con is a convict
the verge is the grass strip at the edge of a road

explanation.surface: An arrangement to meet a crook at the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people coming together at one point gather or come together.

clue.text: They happen to find an opening in two quarters

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south, quarters of the compass
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: People search for a gap across two areas of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrences or happenings are things that take place.

clue.text: Hill split by flood

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
rent means torn apart

explanation.surface: A hill torn apart by floodwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rushing stream of water is a deluge or inundation.
